```{r setup}
source("lkt-vignette-setup.R")
```

The optional `torch` package and LibTorch runtime are required for neural
execution. Install them explicitly with `install.packages("torch")` and
`torch::install_torch(type = "cpu")`. Loading LKT and editing/saving GRU
configurations do not require Torch. Select a CUDA device explicitly if needed;
CUDA execution currently requires `deterministic = FALSE`.

## Architecture and all controls

The default prediction head receives current predictors and a retrieved memory
read. Retrieval uses the previous GRU state and current predictors to query
earlier completed interactions. Only after predicting does the observed answer
enter the recurrent update. The defaults use three 32-unit GRU layers, separate
16-value feature encodings, one filtered retrieval head, and one 128-unit ReLU
prediction-head layer. Explicit arguments select other architectures; LKT's
overall backend default remains LibLinear.

```{r settings}
defaults <- lkt_gru_defaults()
str(defaults)
model <- GRUModel(
  hidden_size = 64, num_layers = 2, gru_dropout = .1,
  head_hidden_sizes = c(32, 16), head_activation = "relu",
  categorical_cols = c("KC..Default.", "Problem.Type"),
  retrieval_filter_cols = c("KC..Default.", "Problem.Type"),
  embedding_dims = c(KC..Default. = 16, Problem.Type = 4),
  numeric_cols = "Item.Difficulty",
  time_col = "CF..Time.", time_units = "seconds",
  input_dropout = .05, head_dropout = .1,
  learning_rate = .001, weight_decay = 1e-4,
  epochs = 100, batch_size = 32, sequence_length = 100,
  early_stopping = TRUE, patience = 10,
  seed = 1, split_seed = 2
)
```

All arguments are documented under `?GRUModel`. `num_layers` controls recurrent
depth; `head_hidden_sizes` controls prediction-head depth and width. Use
`integer(0)` for a linear head. Recurrent dropout requires at least two layers;
input and head dropout are independent. Numeric scaling, vocabularies, and
engineered-feature column schemas are fitted using optimization-training rows.

## A reproducible comparison

This small synthetic example explicitly includes KC and timing information.
Real comparisons should also match the information available to each model,
use the same test students, and distinguish a sequence representation from
engineered summaries of that sequence. A GRU processes event order; elapsed
time is only available when supplied as a predictor.

```{r comparison}
set.seed(41)
d <- data.frame(
  Anon.Student.Id = rep(paste0("s", 1:24), each = 20),
  KC..Default. = rep(c("a", "b"), 240),
  KC..Cluster. = rep(c("skill1", "skill2"), 240),
  CF..Time. = rep(seq(0, by = 300, length.out = 20), 24),
  CF..ansbin. = rbinom(480, 1, .65)
)
d$CF..reltime. <- d$CF..Time.
d <- LKTGRUTimeFeatures(d)
d$fold <- ifelse(d$Anon.Student.Id %in% paste0("s", 21:24), 2, 1)

default_gru <- LKT(
  d, usefolds = 1, components = "KC..Default.", features = "intercept",
  model = GRUModel(time_col = "CF..Time.", epochs = 20), verbose = FALSE
)

terms <- data.frame(
  component = c("KC..Default.", "KC..Default."),
  feature = c("intercept", "recency"), fixed = c("", "0.3")
)
config <- lkt_model_config(
  terms, backend = "GRU", folds = 1,
  gru_options = list(use_lkt_features = TRUE, time_col = "CF..Time.", epochs = 20),
  options = list(verbose = FALSE)
)
engineered_gru <- fit_lkt_config(d, config)

baseline_data <- data.table::as.data.table(d)
baseline_data$fold <- ifelse(seq_len(nrow(d)) %in% default_gru$fit_rows, 1,
                            ifelse(seq_len(nrow(d)) %in% default_gru$validation_rows, 3, 2))
lkt <- LKT(
  baseline_data, usefolds = 1, components = terms$component, features = terms$feature,
  fixedpars = .3, interc = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
)
predict_lkt(default_gru, d, fold = 2, return_stats = TRUE)
predict_lkt(engineered_gru, d, fold = 2, return_stats = TRUE)
predict_lkt(lkt, baseline_data, fold = 2, return_stats = TRUE)
engineered_gru$training_history
lkt_config_call(config)
```

By default, 10% of fitting students (rounded up, at least one) are reserved for
validation. Their outcomes never enter gradients. Test folds are separate.
Explicit `validation_folds` require explicit, disjoint fitting folds.
Within each student, folds must form training, then validation, then evaluation
segments, or the student must belong entirely to one partition. Interleaving
held-out responses before later fitting rows is rejected.

Early stopping and plateau scheduling monitor unweighted validation log loss.
Training can use class/trial weights, but reported predictive metrics remain
unweighted. The best validation weights are restored by default, without an
automatic refit on validation students. `fit_rows`, `validation_rows`, and
`evaluation_rows` record the effective assignment. `loglike` and the null model
refer to optimization-training rows. For fixed-epoch training without validation,
set `validation_fraction = 0, early_stopping = FALSE, scheduler = "none"`.

Engineered nonlinear parameters must already be fixed, estimated independently
on training data if necessary. This backend does not run LKT's outer nonlinear
optimizer, discover KCs, fit random effects, use model-dependent curve features,
or jointly fit latency. Saved terms are inactive when `use_lkt_features = FALSE`.
Raw numeric predictors must be available at prediction time; do not provide
answer-dependent fields such as the current response duration.

## New students, pending trials, and continued histories

```{r continuation}
new_student <- d[d$Anon.Student.Id == "s21", ]
state <- LKTGRUState(engineered_gru)
first <- LKTGRUStep(engineered_gru, state, new_student[1:10, ])
second <- predict_lkt(
  engineered_gru, new_student[11:20, ],
  state = first$state, return_state = TRUE
)
whole <- predict_lkt(engineered_gru, new_student)$predictions
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(c(first$predictions, second$predictions), whole)))

next_trial <- new_student[1, ]
next_trial$CF..ansbin. <- NULL
pending <- LKTGRUStep(engineered_gru, LKTGRUState(engineered_gru), next_trial)
# Supply this trial again with its observed binary answer before advancing.
answered <- LKTGRUStep(engineered_gru, pending$state, new_student[1, ])
```

States are explicit, tied to one fitted model, and returned as new R objects.
They do not change network weights. The default is one history per student.
Set `history_group_cols = c("Anon.Student.Id", "KC..Default.")` for separate
student-by-KC histories; engineered LKT features still follow their own declared
component histories.

An unanswered trial may occur at the end of each history group. It is predicted
without committing a hidden-state update. Unknown categories use the reserved
zero-vector encoding by default; `unknown_levels = "error"` rejects them. Missing
predictors, backwards ordering, or incompatible model states fail explicitly.

Raw-input continuation retains only hidden state and required time/order
metadata. Engineered-feature states additionally retain each student's raw
observed history and rebuild the frozen feature recipe; this has
history-dependent computation and storage costs within that student. Sequence chunk length limits
backpropagation, not how much observed history the fitted model can remember.

## Save, reload, and GUI

```{r save-load}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(list(model = engineered_gru, state = first$state), path)
loaded <- readRDS(path)
continued <- LKTGRUStep(loaded$model, loaded$state, new_student[11:20, ])
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(continued$predictions, second$predictions)))
unlink(path)
```

Weights and hidden states are ordinary named R arrays rather than live Torch
pointers. Configurations, preprocessing, training diagnostics, and software
versions are retained. Architecture changes require a new fitted model.

Open `lkt_gui(config)`, select **GRU**, and use **GRU settings...** to edit every
control. Preview shows the complete generated call without fitting. Save/load
preserves all settings. Vectors use commas; named embedding widths, numeric
transforms, and optimizer/scheduler controls use `name|value` lines. These fields
are parsed as data, never evaluated as R code. There is no automatic search
workflow; vary and save configurations for separate runs.
